cards.text: Moses just finished talking with God at a burning bush, and he's got his orders: Egypt. So first, he goes home to his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He asks him, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.”

cards.question: Jethro tells Moses to stay in Midian a little while longer.

cards.text: Now here's a detail. Back in Midian, the LORD had already told Moses it was safe to go back, and friend, Moses did NOT leave Egypt on good terms.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say it's safe for Moses to go back to Egypt?

answers.text: The men who wanted to kill him are dead
Pharaoh has forgiven what he did years ago
The Israelites have promised to hide him

cards.text: So Moses puts his wife and sons on a donkey and heads for Egypt. A whole family on ONE donkey, and I thought the junk drawer was crowded!

cards.question: Moses heads for Egypt with the ___ of God in his hand.

cards.text: On the road, the LORD gives Moses his instructions. In front of Pharaoh, Moses is to perform ALL the wonders the LORD has put in his power.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses that once Pharaoh sees the wonders, he'll let the people go right away.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses a message for Pharaoh, and it's all about Israel. I bet Pharaoh sees them as nothing but a work crew, and God's about to set him straight.

cards.question: In His message for Pharaoh, what does the LORD call Israel?

cards.text: The message goes on. God told Pharaoh to let His son go so he can worship Him, and Pharaoh has refused.

cards.question: Since Pharaoh refuses to let God's son go, what does the LORD say He'll do?

cards.text: Then, at a lodging place along the way, something shocking happens. The LORD meets Moses and is about to kill him.

cards.question: Moses' life is on the line at that lodging place. Who steps in?

cards.text: Zipporah grabs a flint knife, circumcises her son and touches the foreskin to Moses' feet. She says, “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” and that line is about the circumcision.

cards.question: After Zipporah acts, the LORD lets Moses alone.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the LORD tells Aaron, Moses' brother, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” That's the WHOLE address, no pin, no landmark, and Aaron just GOES.

cards.question: Where do Aaron and Moses finally meet up?

answers.text: On the banks of the Nile

cards.text: Aaron sees his brother and kisses him. The last time I saw my family, a drawer closed between us, so friend, this one gets me right in the dough.

cards.question: Moses keeps the signs to himself and lets Aaron find out at the big meeting.

cards.text: Then Moses and Aaron gather all the elders of the Israelites. I bet Moses has been sweating this exact moment since the burning bush.

cards.question: With the elders gathered, who relays everything the LORD said to Moses?
While Aaron does the talking, Moses performs the ___ before the people.
After hearing the LORD's words and seeing the signs, how do the people respond?
When the people hear that the LORD has seen their affliction, they ___ down and ___.

cards.text: The elders are bowing, the brothers are back together, and Moses still has a meeting with Pharaoh on the calendar. That's where we'll leave it, friend, because this story is FAR from done.

findings.problem: The card brings in facts from outside the passage: the burning bush (Exodus 3:2) and Jethro as 'the priest of Midian' (Exodus 3:1). Neither has a reference, and the card cites only Exodus 4:18.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'Moses did NOT leave Egypt on good terms' is an outside fact (Exodus 2:15, Pharaoh sought to kill Moses) with no reference. The card cites only Exodus 4:19.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'On the road' adds a time and place the text doesn't give. Exodus 4:21 says only that the LORD instructed Moses, 'When you go back to Egypt…', and doesn't say where Moses was when he heard it.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: No card ever tells the baker that the LORD says He will harden Pharaoh's heart (Exodus 4:21), and that is a key detail of the passage. The true or false card only shows that Pharaoh won't let the people go right away. The hardening itself is never told.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'God's about to set him straight' gives a reason for God's message that Exodus 4:22 doesn't state. It presents the message as God correcting Pharaoh's view of Israel. 'I bet' marks only Pharaoh's view as a guess. The purpose given to God is stated as fact.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This is a 'who' question, but the wrong answer 'The oldest elder' isn't a real person or detail from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Moses' isn't false everywhere in the passage. In Exodus 4:28, Moses tells Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, so a baker could argue that Moses relays the LORD's words.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: 'The elders are bowing' narrows who bowed. Exodus 4:30-31 says Moses performed the signs 'before the people' and 'they' believed and worshiped. The text calls them the people, not specifically the elders.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The last verse (Exodus 4:31) is already asked on cards 8 and 9, but this closing card opens by recapping earlier moments: the bowing, the brothers reunited, and the meeting with Pharaoh from 4:21. It should be just the 'story isn't over' line, and it shouldn't cite 4:31 as if it tells something new.

The humor is thin and mostly mild. Stop 1, cards 7 through 16, has no humor at all, including the message to Pharaoh (cards 9 through 12), which could hold a laugh without muddying a fact. Most of the jokes that are there, like the donkey line, the work crew line and the 'no pin' address, read as pleasant rather than laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
